subject: Unexpected token spike on 2026-07-18 — request for forensics and provisional rollback
messages:
From: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@bluehaven.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 23:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden 18k token spike on 7/18 — please investigate / provisional rollback?

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a massive, unexpected usage spike in our July 18th billing window — roughly 280k tokens (~$18,200) above our normal baseline. I've attached a small sample (bluehaven-usage-sample-20260718.csv) with a clear cluster around 03:02-03:08 UTC.

We did a controlled migration of a small microservice that morning, and we suspect something replayed requests, but this pattern doesn't match anything on our side. Can Redwood confirm whether these requests are present in server logs as unique request IDs or whether there's evidence of duplication on your ingest path?

We need:
- A quick forensics summary of what caused the spike (duplication, replay, anomalous client behavior, etc.)
- If the excess is due to a cloud/proxy/retry issue, a provisional rollback/credit while we investigate (invoice due next week).

Attachments: bluehaven-usage-sample-20260718.csv (CSV with timestamps and request ids - first 50 rows).

Appreciate an expedited look — Ana (cc: ops@bluehaven.com)

--
Ana Ruiz
Head of Platform
Bluehaven Systems
ana.ruiz@bluehaven.com

Ben / Marissa — forwarding a customer billing escalation (Bluehaven). They have a tight invoice timeline and are seeing a concentrated token spike overnight on 2026-07-18.

Quick asks:
- Can billing run a per-request-id dedupe and confirm whether tokens for those timestamps are duplicated at the ingestion layer? If so, what's the best estimate of billable vs duplicated tokens?
- If we confirm platform-side duplication/replay, please advise on provisional credit / invoice hold options and the operational steps to apply a one-time credit.
- I'll add Neha for compliance/region flagging (EU VAT not relevant here but keep on the loop).

Attachments: forwarding the customer's sample for context.

Timing: customer needs an initial answer today if possible. I don't want to promise credits without evidence — please prioritize forensics and then propose a remediation number to offer while we complete the investigation.

Thanks — Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@bluehaven.com>, Ops Eng <ops@bluehaven.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden 18k token spike on 7/18 — request for forensics and provisional rollback?

Thanks for flagging — I've pulled the raw ingestion traces for Bluehaven for 2026-07-18 02:50–03:20 UTC. Initial finding: there is a high volume of requests that share the same client-side request IDs in short bursts (see sample lines attached). That pattern looks consistent with a retry loop at the load balancer / client-side proxy, not internal Redwood duplication.

What I ran:
- Matched customer's sample against our request_id index (we keep the first-seen fingerprint).
- Checked our edge ingress for retries: we see repeated identical request_id and identical body/payload signatures within sub-second windows coming from the same IP block (x.x.67.0/24).
- Verified KV cache behavior: no cache evictions would have caused replays here.

Preliminary estimate: ~260k tokens (approx $16,800) appear to be repeat/replay of earlier requests from the same session cluster. Baseline legitimate usage for the window is ~22k tokens.

Proposed short-term remediation:
- Provisionally apply a one-time credit of $15,000 to cover the majority of the excess (covers ~89% of the suspected replay).
- Put the outstanding invoice on hold while we complete full logs handoff and allow Bluehaven to investigate their proxy configuration.

I'm attaching: "redwood-ingest-sample-20260718.txt" (first 200 matching request ids), and will prepare a credit memo draft for Marissa to issue.

Marissa — if you approve, please create a provisional credit memo and route to accounts-receivable. I recommend a manual adjustment on invoice INV-20260701-BH to reflect the credit; we can reconcile final numbers after the customer's internal postmortem.

Soojin — please ask Bluehaven if they can share any LB/proxy logs (timestamps + request ids) for 03:00–03:10 UTC to correlate.

Ben

--
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks Ben — and thanks Soojin for looping folks in. We've attached a small subset of our LB logs (bluehaven-migration-log-20260718.txt) that show repeated upstream retries from 03:01:58 to 03:08:14 UTC (same request ids).

We appreciate the provisional approach; authorizing the $15,000 credit sounds reasonable while we finish our postmortem. Please let us know what you need to confirm the memo and any short form we should sign to acknowledge the provisional adjustment.

Also: could Redwood add a short note to the invoice stating "provisional one-time adjustment pending final reconciliation" so our finance team doesn't auto-pay the disputed amount?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Ana
